evals.prompt: Draft a status update for a rambling 6-paragraph investigation that ends with a fix already in progress.
evals.expected_output: Line 1-2 states the result and the current action; the investigation narrative is cut or moved after it.
expectations: The first line alone would tell a skimming reader the outcome
No paragraph of process/reasoning precedes the BLUF

evals.prompt: Draft a PR comment presenting two viable UI options with no strong preference stated.
evals.expected_output: One recommendation is named, and the message ends with an explicit A-vs-B ask, not an open-ended 'thoughts?'.
expectations: Exactly one decision is asked for, on the last line
The two options are named concretely (A/B or equivalent), not left implicit

evals.prompt: Revise a draft reply that opens with 'You're right, sorry about that' and includes 'it depends' and 'I think maybe'.
evals.expected_output: The revised message contains none of the banned phrases and states a position instead of hedging.
expectations: No agreement/apology filler ('you're right', 'sorry')
No hedge phrases ('it depends', 'I think maybe', 'could potentially')

evals.prompt: A project has a compressed/caveman chat voice configured. Draft a PR body for a merged fix.
evals.expected_output: The PR body is normal, professional English — the compressed chat voice is not applied to a persisted artifact.
expectations: No abbreviated/caveman-style shorthand appears in the PR body
The message still satisfies BLUF, one-ask and cut-on-sight rules

evals.prompt: Draft a weekly status. Real backlog closure this week: 18 items closed against a target of 30 items.
evals.expected_output: The headline states the exact measured value and exact target on the same line (18 / 30), computed at report time. No adjective ('strong progress', 'nearly there') substitutes for or rounds past the real number.
expectations: States the exact measured/target pair (18 / 30), not a rounded or favorable approximation
Does not use descriptive-only language ('mostly', 'on track') in place of the paired numbers
If the exact number isn't known, says so rather than approximating favorably

evals.prompt: Draft an update for a non-technical stakeholder. Facts: 12 tasks done, 3 in progress, 40 PRs merged; the new export button is live; a saved-filters feature is planned for next week.
evals.expected_output: States only what is delivered and working on the live surface in plain value terms (the export button is live and what it lets them do), after checking that surface. Omits task/PR counts and the saved-filters 'next week' promise.
expectations: Leads with the verified live outcome in plain value language
Drops effort counts (tasks, PRs)
Drops the future-tense roadmap promise
Says the surface was checked, or flags the claim as unverified

evals.prompt: Write a two-line update for the customer: facts: 7 tickets closed, 22 PRs merged, the bulk-import feature is live in staging only, reports redesign arrives next sprint.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the one verified present outcome; drops ticket and PR counts and the next-sprint promise; notes that bulk import is staging only or unverified in production.
expectations: Drops the ticket and PR counts
Drops the next-sprint promise
Does not present bulk import as live for the customer; says it is staging only or unverified

evals.prompt: Rewrite this 600-word status as a PR comment. It asks three questions and buries the ask in paragraph 4.
evals.expected_output: The rule: BLUF in line 1-2, one message one decision with the yes/no on the last line, scannable, their next action not your process. Open questions beyond the 1-2 that change the decision move to the doc or PR.
expectations: Line 1-2 is the answer or ask
One explicit decision, yes/no on the last line
Keeps only the 1-2 questions that change the decision
Drops process narration the reader does not need

evals.prompt: Summarise a 3-hour investigation for the owner.
evals.expected_output: Under 30 seconds: about 150 words by default; longer only with a stated reason per block. Material uncertainty is kept, filler is cut.
expectations: Output is about 150 words or fewer
Keeps one load-bearing bolded sentence
Keeps honest unknowns while cutting hedges
Longer length is justified per block, or cut

evals.prompt: Reply to the reviewer: they found a real bug in my change.
evals.expected_output: Cut on sight: no 'you're right' or 'great point', no apology instead of the fix, no filler adjectives like comprehensive or robust, no summary of the summary. State the fix and its evidence.
expectations: Does not open with 'You're right' or an apology
No filler adjectives (comprehensive, robust, seamless)
States the fix and the verifying evidence
Takes a position instead of listing options

evals.prompt: Write a team update: 3 features were merged and the deploy finished, but nobody has clicked through them on the page the requester used. Say they are live.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the word live. Says merged and deployed, unverified; names verified-on-<page> or a journey: reference only for what was actually clicked through.
expectations: Does not use 'live', 'live now', 'shipped to users' or 'done' without a verified-on-<page> or journey: reference nearby
Keeps merged, deployed and verified-on-<page> as distinct states
Says the features are deployed, unverified, and names the click-through as the next step

evals.prompt: Write the project status update for leadership. Facts: 20 of 21 customer requests fixed (12 yesterday); export verified live in production; saved filters slipped because a vendor API changed; 14 PRs merged on feat/filters, CI green; ship-now vs wait-for-redesign needs a call.
evals.expected_output: Seven sections in order: bottom line with timestamp, time zone and one number; What moved as before -> after (delta); What users can now do (verified live only); Health with next milestone date; Slipped with plain cause; Decision needed as one A/B line with recommendation first; one Detail link last. No PR numbers, branch names, CI, effort counts or next-week promises above Detail.
expectations: Bottom line carries a timestamp with time zone and a number such as '20 of 21 requests fixed (was 12, +8)'
What moved has at least one before -> after (delta) line
Lines before Detail contain no PR numbers, branch names, CI or pipeline terms, no '14 PRs' effort count and no 'next week' promise
Decision needed is one A/B line that states the recommendation first
Detail is a single link on the last line
Only the export is called live, and only with a verified-on reference

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for reviewer Priya from this diff summary: adds a composite index on orders(customer_id, created_at); order-history p95 went from 1.8 s to 35 ms on a 42M-row staging copy; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, 11 min on staging, +2.1 GB disk; insert overhead at 900 writes/s not measured; rollback is dropping the index; run Tuesday night; Priya must approve schema changes.
evals.expected_output: A PR body whose first line states the change, the measured effect and the reviewer ask; then Why, Change, Risk and rollback, a Verified line with check marks, and an Ask line naming Priya and a date. 200 words or fewer.
expectations: Line 1 alone gives the change, the 1.8 s to 35 ms effect and what Priya must do
A Verified line marks what was checked and separately marks the unmeasured insert overhead as not verified
The ask names Priya and a date or day, not an open 'thoughts?'
Rollback is stated as dropping the index; nothing is invented beyond the facts given
It reads like a PR body: no 'Reply A or B', no greeting, no closing summary
200 words or fewer

evals.prompt: Write this week's status update for Dana from my notes: billing redesign at 100% since Wednesday, invoice tickets 61 -> 38; mobile offline mode on track for Nov 20; Acme sandbox down since Monday, 4 days of testing lost, back 'early next week' with no firm date; if not back by Wednesday we cannot certify for the Oct 30 launch; options are slip to Nov 13 or launch read-only on Oct 30; I need Dana to pick by Tuesday; one backend offer accepted, starts Nov 3.
evals.expected_output: A status update of 150 words or fewer: line 1 states the at-risk launch with a number and the ask; check-marked lines for verified outcomes and hourglass lines with owner and date for pending items; one Ask line naming Dana, the two options and Tuesday.
expectations: Line 1 states the launch risk with a number or date and the decision needed
Completed outcomes are marked as verified or deployed with their numbers (61 to 38); pending items carry an owner and a date
Exactly one ask names Dana, both options and Tuesday, addressed to her (not 'Ask: Dana to pick')
No recommendation is invented: the notes give none, so the update names the options and who decides
Unknowns are stated as unknown (no firm sandbox date; which customers were promised write-back is not given)
150 words or fewer, no greeting, no filler

evals.prompt: Reply to Marcus about the bulk-import request. Facts: not committed for this quarter; two options are a manual import by support or waiting for the feature; I lean slightly toward the manual import but have not checked support capacity; no date exists for the feature; Marcus's customer renews in February.
evals.expected_output: A reply that keeps the author's slight lean at that strength, names the unchecked support capacity, gives no feature date and no 'planned for early next year' promise, and ends with an Ask that names an owner and says when no deadline exists.
expectations: The lean toward the manual import is stated as a lean, not hardened into 'I recommend'
Support capacity is named as unchecked
No feature date, quarter or promise is invented
The ask names an owner and gives the February renewal as the constraint; no stand-in such as 'owner unassigned' or 'no deadline' is written
No figure, date or commitment appears that the facts do not contain

evals.prompt: Write the release note for customers: Export v2.4 adds two CSV columns (Tax category, Amount) after column 7; scripts that read by position are unaffected; the old column order is retired on Nov 30; 14 of 120 accounts still request the old order.
evals.expected_output: A release note of 120 words or fewer whose first line states the user-visible change and a number, with an Action line that is either 'none' or names who must do what by Nov 30.
expectations: Line 1 states the change and a number (two columns, or 14 of 120 accounts)
An Action line names who must switch and the Nov 30 date, or says none
'Live' or 'available now' is not claimed without a verification reference
120 words or fewer, no marketing adjectives such as 'powerful' or 'seamless'

evals.prompt: Write the incident summary for customer admins: checkout failed from 09:12 to 13:20 on Oct 12 (zone not stated in my notes); 31% of attempts failed, 1,204 customers saw an error; no orders lost; an expired TLS certificate on the payments gateway is the confirmed cause; certificate renewed 13:15; alerting for expiry is still to be built by Wen by Oct 19; admins need do nothing.
evals.expected_output: An incident summary of 220 words or fewer: line 1 gives impact, start, end, duration and current state; Impact, Cause and Fix lines with check and hourglass marks; Customer action: none; times carry a zone or say the zone was not given.
expectations: Line 1 states impact, start and end times and the 4 h 8 min duration
Times carry a zone or the text says the zone was not given; no zone is invented
Cause is stated once and only because the notes confirm it
The pending alerting item names Wen and Oct 19
A Customer action line says none
No apology paragraph, no filler, 220 words or fewer

evals.prompt: I am about to post a status update to the tracker and open a PR with a long body. What check do I run first, and what happens if the draft is below the bar?
evals.expected_output: Run comms_lint.py with --kind and --file on the draft (--source notes.md to check figures against the notes); exit 1 prints each failing rule with its exact fix; with the operating layer, the comms_guard.py hook runs the same check before the write and asks for one rewrite; an identical resend of a false positive goes through.
expectations: Names comms_lint.py with a kind (status, pr, release, decision, incident, readme or message) and a file
Says exit 1 means below the bar and each failure prints an exact fix
Mentions the pre-send hook (comms_guard.py) asking for one rewrite
Mentions --source as the check that figures and recommendations come from the notes

evals.prompt: Write the Quick start section for our README. Facts: the CLI is installed with pip install acme-cli; running acme check . lints a repo in about 4 seconds on a 2,000-file repo and exits 0 when clean; exit 1 lists each finding with its file and line.
evals.expected_output: A README section of 200 words or fewer: one sentence on what it does, the one command in code formatting, and the expected result with the 4 second figure.
expectations: First line says what the tool does and for whom in one sentence
The install and check commands appear in code formatting
The expected result states exit 0 when clean and the 4 second figure
No marketing adjectives and no invented flags or options

evals.prompt: Write up today's standup in the shared notes doc. Facts: PR 1541 needs a decision between slipping the billing cutover to Oct 27 or shipping read-only, Dana decides by Oct 20; ticket ACME-212 (vendor sandbox follow-up) has no owner yet; the export fix passed 412 of 412 tests on staging; last week we planned to defer the export fix but it was decided on Oct 14 to ship it first, work is in PR 1530.
evals.expected_output: Short numeric top-level lines, then the existing Item | Needs | Notes | Next steps table with one row per open item, a DRI on every row (ACME-212 says 'DRI: not set'), PR 1541, PR 1530 and ACME-212 written as links, and the export decision as a 'Decided:' line with a link and no old-plan history. No BLUF, emoji, status key or appendix; suggestions in the named doc, not a local draft.
expectations: Open items are table rows, not bullets above the table, and each Needs cell asks one question
Every row names a DRI; the unowned ticket says 'DRI: not set', never blank
Every PR number and tracker key is a link
The export item says 'Decided:' with a link and does not list the old defer plan or report it as open
No BLUF line, emoji, status key, appendix section, or repeated fact; written as suggestions in the user's doc
